title: AI-ECG mortality alerts reduce 90-day deaths in a randomized trial in Taiwan
summary: A Taiwanese randomized trial involving 15,965 patients found 90-day mortality of 3.6% with AI-ECG alerts versus 4.3% with usual care.
account: An academic medical center and a community hospital in Taiwan tested AI-ECG alerts with 39 physicians and 15,965 patients. Patients were randomly assigned to AI-assisted care or usual care. Ninety-day all-cause mortality, the primary endpoint, was 3.6% versus 4.3%, respectively: hazard ratio 0.83, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.70–0.99. The prespecified high-risk subgroup had a hazard ratio of 0.69 (0.53–0.90). The trial covered ECGs collected from December 15, 2021, through April 30, 2022. Longer-term survival and generalizability to other health systems remain uncertain.
purpose: Identify patients at high risk of death and prompt timely clinical assessment.
system: AI-ECG mortality prediction and physician alert system
developer: National Defense Medical Center and Tri-Service General Hospital research team
deployer: An academic medical center and a community hospital in Taiwan

ratings.reason: The randomized trial found lower all-cause mortality with AI-assisted care, supporting a survival benefit for patients.

ai_role.statement: A convolutional neural network assessed ECGs and sent high-risk alerts to physicians. Clinicians selected further assessment and treatment. The trial evaluated this combined care pathway. The precise mechanism of the survival improvement remains uncertain.

evidence.citation: Lin CS, Liu WT, Tsai DJ, et al. (2024). Nature Medicine 30:1461–1470. doi:10.1038/s41591-024-02961-4. Randomized trial conducted by the system's research team. Figures 1–4; Methods; Supplementary Note 1 and Figure 1.

claim_chains.finding: Patient-level allocation preceded treatment. The registration was supplied by the sponsor and is not a regulatory finding. All-cause mortality within 90 days was the prespecified primary endpoint.
The trial used the team's survival neural network described by Tsai et al. (2023), trained on 451,950 ECGs. The actual deployed weights are proprietary.
This is a secondary analysis of the randomized trial. Its estimates are costs per death averted over 90 days, not lifetime value or a direct measurement of savings.
